messages:
Sue (AE): quick heads-up — Prospect requires a POC delivered entirely offline (sneakernet / USB shipment). No egress from their DC. They want an on-prem bundle + install runbook. Main asks: packaging approach, delta vs full updates, signing & attestation, upgrade cadence, and one-time pricing for offline bundling. Can SE + Ops weigh in?

Rahul (SE): Yep, we can do this. A few technical checkpoints first: what OS/container runtime are they on (RHEL8/Ubuntu20.04 + containerd/docker)? Do they allow our operator to run as a privileged DaemonSet? Also need to confirm whether k8s is present or this is a single-node VM.

Beth (Ops): For POC we can create a trimmed "minibundle". Full image set is ~12GB uncompressed; minibundle (core runtime + model artifact subset) down to ~2.1GB. For USB transfer we usually chunk the tarball into 2GB parts and provide a signed manifest + checksums. Recommend the customer do an integrity check post-copy.

Mike (Security): Security notes: we need to know if customer mandates keys live in their HSM/KMS or if our shipped signing key is acceptable for POC. Also clarify TLS root CA acceptance — will they import our CA, or must we sign with their root? Telemetry must be disabled by default for air-gapped installs.

Alex (AM): On pricing — typical approach is: one-off offline packaging fee + per-POC support hours + SOW for on-site ops if we staff the install. Ballpark: $6k packaging + $2k/day for onsite SEs. Will confirm with finance if they want a reduced trial rate.

Rahul (SE): Operational constraints / recommended workflow:
- Provide target host inventory (OS, k8s, available GPUs, disk free)
- We build a signed bundle and deliver SHA256+signature file
- Customer copies bundle to staging host, runs installer with --airgap flag
- Installer verifies signature, unpacks, loads images into local registry
- Post-install we run a short smoke test (token generation, simple prompt)

Example verification we ask them to run on the host:
```
sha256sum redwood-bundle.tar.gz > redwood-bundle.tar.gz.sha256
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify redwood_pubkey.pem -signature redwood-bundle.sig redwood-bundle.tar.gz
```

Beth (Ops): For upgrades: for POC we can allow a 3-month delta cadence (smaller diffs), production recommendation 6–12 months with urgent hotfix windows. Deltas require us to ship a delta patch generator and a signed delta manifest; offline diffs are more error-prone if base images diverge.

Sue (AE): Customer also asked about SBOM and provenance for internal auditors. Can we provide SBOM + signed manifest?

Mike (Security): Yes, we supply SPDX SBOM for each bundle and sign it. For regulated customers we can include notarization metadata and per-artifact hashes. Need to confirm retention/version policy in SOW.

Alex (AM): @Rahul @Beth any ops blockers for delivery timeline? Customer wants POC next-week window (7 business days).

Rahul (SE): Tight but doable if we get host inventory and model selection today. I can prep a minibundle build script and smoke tests. Need 24–36h for build + signing.

Beth (Ops): Ops can produce the chunked USB images in 48 hours once we have the build artifact. We also need a contact for courier chain-of-custody (who we hand USBs to).

shipbot: Created ticket INF-3782 for "sneakernet bundle creation" and attached build checklist.

Sue (AE): Great — I'll gather host inventory and courier contact. For pricing I'll confirm whether they want a reduced pilot SOW.

Alex (AM): I'll loop in finance for the 6k packaging + any discount.

Mike (Security): I'll draft a short security addendum: HSM requirements, telemetry disabled, SBOM + signed manifests, and CA import instructions. Will post in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:

Rahul (SE): Cool — once I have the inventory I'll post the exact commands + expected logs for verification. :eyes:

Beth (Ops): tagging runbook template: /runbooks/airgap-sneakernet-install.md (internal)

Sue (AE): Thanks everyone — will update the prospect and come back with inventory later today.
